tier_reason: The README gives first-party ratios against the base64 crate: decode is 2-2.5x faster and encode 1.2-1.5x faster with AVX2 on Zen 2. It also has a decode graph in ns, and the criterion bench code (benches/bench.rs, base64 0.21.5 as 'baseline') is public. No CPU model is given and the exact bench flags are not stated, so it cannot be A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc nightly (rust-toolchain.toml); README recommends -Ctarget-cpu=native -Zbuild-std for max performance but does not state these were the exact bench flags
corrections.workload: Criterion benchmark (benches/bench.rs) on 256 test vectors of small inputs (graph covers ~0-500 bytes), vb64 vs base64 crate 0.21.5, AVX2 on an unspecified AMD Zen 2 machine
corrections.caveats: No exact CPU model (only 'Zen 2 machine'); first-party benchmark; the README graph shows decode only (average ns per call vs input size up to ~500 bytes), so there are no large-buffer throughput numbers; with only SSSE3 the README says decode is even with base64 and encode is much worse; baseline base64 crate is scalar; requires nightly (std::simd)

notes: The last commit on main is 2023-11-26. GitHub's pushed_at of 2024-02-08 is not a commit date, so maintenance_status changes from abandoned to stale (about 2.8 years). The HN thread 'Designing a SIMD Algorithm from Scratch' (441 points) is confirmed via Algolia, and the star count (90) and Apache-2.0 license are confirmed.

tier_reason: SMHasher3 is a well-known independent suite. Its results summary lists a5hash at 26.91 avg cycles (1-32 byte keys) against wyhash 29.31 and XXH-64 52.60. The summary and the raw a5hash.txt give no CPU model or compiler (only a nominal '@ 3.5 ghz' conversion), so it cannot be A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: SMHasher3 results summary: a5hash small-key (1-32 bytes) avg 26.91 cycles/hash vs wyhash 29.31 and XXH-64 52.60 (about 8% and 49% fewer cycles, derived from page data). On bulk data, a5hash is slower than both baselines: 2.63 bytes/cycle vs wyhash 6.98 and XXH-64 3.99 (a5hash-128 does 6.92). The author's README (first-party SMHasher3 run on Xeon E-2386G) gives 11.50 cycles/hash small-key vs XXH3-64 21.31 and rapidhash (wyhash-derived) 18.10. It also gives about 11 cycles/hash for 0-64 byte strings on Zen 5 and 15 GB/s bulk on Ryzen 9950X.
corrections.hardware: Unstated in the SMHasher3 summary (raw file only converts at a nominal 3.5 GHz); author's README comparison table ran on Xeon E-2386G (Rocket Lake), AlmaLinux 9.3; author's headline numbers are from Zen 5 / Ryzen 9950X
corrections.caveats: Same author as komihash (already catalogued); the win is small-key only: bulk throughput on the SMHasher3 page (2.63 B/cycle) is below wyhash (6.98) and XXH-64 (3.99), and the author says bulk is 'intentionally moderately fast'; the SMHasher3 page gives no compiler or CPU; SMHasher3 tested a5hash v5.21 while the repo is now at v5.25; the README's own comparison table (Xeon E-2386G, SMHasher3 commit 7be7e9e) gives no compiler or flags

notes: The numbers on the SMHasher3 page match the record exactly, and a5hash passes 250/250 tests while wyhash fails 15 and XXH-64 fails 9. The README has a first-party table against XXH3-64 and rapidhash that the record said was missing, so it was added. Metadata is confirmed: MIT, 51 stars, last commit 2025-12-19, active.

tier_reason: The SMHasher3 independent results summary lists AquaHash at 15.84 bytes/cycle bulk against XXH-64 3.99 and wyhash 6.98. No compiler or CPU model is stated there, so it cannot be A. The README graph against xxhash64/FarmHash on Skylake is first-party, has no flags, and has no public bench code.

corrections.claimed_speedup: SMHasher3 results summary: AquaHash bulk 15.84 bytes/cycle vs XXH-64 3.99 and wyhash 6.98 (about 4x and 2.3x, derived from page data). The margin over XXH3-64 (12.82) is only about 1.24x, derived from page data. On small keys (1-32 bytes, avg cycles) AquaHash scores 34.31, which beats XXH-64 (52.60) but is slower than wyhash (29.31). Own README: 'substantially outperforms most common hash functions at all key sizes', about 15 bytes/cycle bulk, and a cycles-per-hash graph up to 256-byte keys vs xxhash64 and FarmHash on Skylake.
corrections.caveats: Fails 55 of 250 SMHasher3 tests (195/250 passed), a notable quality concern despite the speed; needs AES-NI; no commits since the 2019-03-06 v1.0 release; the README graph (Skylake) gives no compiler or flags and has no public bench harness; the bulk lead shrinks to about 1.24x against the modern XXH3-64

notes: The last commit is 2019-03-06; the record's 2019-08-12 was GitHub's pushed_at. The caveats 'predates wyhash' (the wyhash GitHub repo was created 2019-03-06, the same day) and 'never reached a stated v2.0' (no source mentions v2.0) were unsupported and have been removed. License Apache-2.0, 85 stars and abandoned status are confirmed.
